text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Prime Minister Alain Juppe presented his platform to the parliamentary majority yesterday, denied preparing further austerity measures for after the upcoming parliamentary election, but confirmed the state would have to cut some of its spending, and stressed planned tax cuts. (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro, L'Agefi, Liberation, The International Herald Tribune).
LES ECHOS
-- Volume of transactions in real-estate rose in 1996, and foreign investors are back on the market, according to report by Credit Foncier.
-- Generale des Eaux in property joint-venture with Caisse des Depots et des Placements de Quebec
-- Insurer AGF to launch some four billion francs worth of subordinated convertible bonds, to restructure its debt.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Partial privatisation of France Telecom postponed until June 5, after the parliamentary election.
-- Credit Lyonnais to sell its 58.6 percent stake in Italy's Credito Bergamasco.
-- Caisse des Depots et Consignations posts a 4 billion francs profit for 1996.
L'AGEFI
-- Prime Minister Alain Juppe expected to send letters to ministers detailing spending for 1998, budget spending is expected to be frozen to 1997 levels in constant francs.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE

-- Government announces intention to freeze 1998 state spending to 1997 levels, which would represent a two percent drop, in real terms. Public deficit for 1998 is forecast around 260 billion francs, from an expected 284 billion this year.
-- Unions and management at British Airways TAT-Air Liberte reach agreement on pilots' status, other staff to resume negotiations.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Privatisation of Thomson-CSF may be jeopardised by a possible change in government after the upcoming parliamentary election.
-- Pilots at former Air Inter airline to strike Friday and Saturday against the terms of their integration into the Air France group.
-- Court rules BNP bank to give compensation to a small firm it had led to bankruptcy by suppressing its overdraft without notice.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- France Telecom sale pushed back to June to prevent it from being hurt by doubts over the outcome of the vote.
